free_tier.stated: USD 10 of starting credit on signup, roughly 60 hours of the default 2 vCPU/2 GiB instance; OpenCode Zen models ending in -free need no provider key.
free_tier.notes: The USD 10 is a one-time starting credit, not a recurring allowance; it is consumed by sandbox compute at the published per-second rates.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a sandbox, not an object
per_object_cap.notes: Up to 20 input files and 32 repositories per request are documented; no storage object cap is published.

retention.stated: A chat's sandbox stops when a turn ends and resumes for the next one; files and agent session survive. Artifact download URLs are presigned for about ten minutes and renewable.

egress.terms: Not published as a volume or price; the sandbox runs on the vendor's boxes and artifacts return as presigned URLs.

interface_detail: One REST endpoint POST /api/v1/chat plus /chat/async, streaming server-sent events and a chat_id for a durable multi-turn sandbox; MCP servers and repository tokens are declared in the request.
tooling: A single HTTP POST with a JSON body and an API key; no SDK or daemon is required.
chaining: Runs can be driven from scripts, CI, cron or a Slack bot, and model tokens bill to the caller's own provider key with no Epho markup.

limits.value: USD 10 starting credit on signup; a turn is refused with 402 at zero balance
teams start with five active turns; extra turns queue at no cost until a slot opens
up to 32 repositories and 20 input files per request

limits_note: A run is metered from boot to teardown and stops when the run does; one live turn per chat.
binding_note: The USD 10 starting credit is the first allowance to run out; the five-turn active limit is a concurrency gate that queues rather than stops work.

identity_cost.detail: A team API key is required and, per a third-party review, sign-up involves email verification. The exact fields of the registration form were not read: the app.epho.io registration page redirected to sign-in and presented a login wall to every reader.

reliability_note: A dropped stream does not kill a run: events are persisted and replayed on reconnect; the platform re-queues a run on a fallback sandbox backend when a box dies mid-run.
confidence_note: Per-second rates and credit are quoted from the vendor home page read on 2026-11-25; the email-verification step is reported by a third party because the registration page was a login wall.
